nodes.label: packages/core strict determinism invariant
nodes.rationale: No Math.random/Date.now/clock in core: replaying an action log must reconstruct the exact game state for persistence and server-side reconstruction; any non-determinism would silently break this.

nodes.label: LOS symmetry-by-construction
nodes.rationale: los.ts canonicalizes endpoint order before Bresenham raycast so line-of-sight is symmetric by construction; must not be broken.

nodes.label: Fog of war is structural, not applicative
nodes.rationale: The match Durable Object holds GameState and both PlayerKnowledge and sends each player only their own viewFor(); a client cannot receive what the DO never sends, so fog cannot be bypassed via devtools.
nodes.norm_label: fog of war is structural, not applicative

nodes.label: Durable Object must hibernate
nodes.rationale: A DO holding an open WebSocket without hibernating costs ~20000x more with no functional difference; must be covered by a dedicated test.

nodes.label: Global matchmaking Durable Object
nodes.rationale: A second, global DO serves as the matchmaking queue; its single-threading eliminates double pairing by construction.

nodes.label: D1 action log is the source of truth
nodes.rationale: The DO's in-memory state is a reconstructible cache; the D1 action log is authoritative, relying entirely on core's determinism invariant.
nodes.norm_label: d1 action log is the source of truth

nodes.label: Rules versioned per match, not per connection
nodes.rationale: A match started under ruleset v3 finishes under v3; since the client target is a downloadable Electron app with unlimited thinking time, matches span deployments and old clients embed old core.
nodes.norm_label: rules versioned per match, not per connection

nodes.label: One branch = one full hosted environment
nodes.rationale: Hosted branches are explicitly selected via .github/deploy-environments.json, never auto-deployed, so environment population is decided rather than incidental; a branch touching core changes rules and must not be tested against main's.
nodes.norm_label: one branch = one full hosted environment

nodes.label: src/theme.ts sole color-value file
nodes.rationale: apps/web/src/theme.ts is the only client file allowed to contain a color value, enforced mechanically by an ESLint rule rather than convention.

nodes.label: Height as Wall (not a flag)
nodes.rationale: docs/design.md section 5.1: un mur est une case haute, jamais un flag booléen — la hauteur seule bloque la ligne de vue, ce qui unifie relief et occultation dans un seul modèle de données.

nodes.label: LOS Canonical-Order Symmetry
nodes.rationale: Bresenham depends on traversal direction along diagonals; without canonicalizing endpoint order before rasterizing, A could see B without B seeing A — unacceptable in a 1v1 hidden-information game, so the pair is sorted into a fixed order before tracing (docs/design.md section 5.1).

nodes.label: Verticality Movement Rules
nodes.rationale: docs/design.md section 5.3: descendre est libre et illimité ; monter un niveau consomme le tour entier et exige d'être déjà collé au relief (pas d'enchaînement marche+grimpe) ; un dénivelé de 2+ est infranchissable — encode une asymétrie voulue entre attaque/déplacement montant et descendant.

nodes.label: Fog of War Ghost Memory
nodes.rationale: docs/design.md section 5.4: un souvenir de pièce adverse n'est effacé que lorsqu'il est contredit (case revue vide) — sinon il persiste, car le joueur n'a aucun moyen de savoir que la pièce a bougé hors de sa vue.

nodes.label: One Action = One Piece's Full Turn
nodes.rationale: docs/design.md section 6/3.1: la capture de mêlée est instantanée et résolue dans la même action que le déplacement qui l'a permise, comme aux échecs ; `to` peut valoir la case de départ pour exprimer 'frapper sans bouger' sans déduire la capture du seul contact.
nodes.norm_label: one action = one piece's full turn

nodes.label: One Piece Type = One Class
nodes.rationale: PieceType porte le comportement (mouvement, vision, frappe) et sert de point d'extension par héritage, tandis que Piece reste une donnée inerte sérialisable — sépare ce qui traverse le réseau/log de rejeu de ce qui définit les règles versionnées par partie.

nodes.label: Server-Side Fog Redaction
nodes.rationale: docs/design.md section 5.4 / architecture: le fog of war doit être appliqué à la source (le futur serveur), pas seulement caché à l'affichage, sinon il est contournable via les devtools — PlayerView ne transporte que ce qui est réellement dans la LOS ou mémorisé.
